Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, they all appear to be dated around March 2025 but with slightly different histories. Let me examine the patterns:

Example 1 (2025-03-28):
- History starts at 68.50 and ends at 68.54 (last 18 days)
- The history shows a general downward trend from peak 73.44 on day 11-12, bottoming around 68.54
- Model forecasts are generally higher than true outcomes
- Looking at the first few days: model forecasts ~68.92 vs true 68.80 (overestimated by +0.12)
- By day 5: model 67.74 vs true 66.06 (overestimated by +1.68)
- By day 10: model 65.56 vs true 62.12 (overestimated by +3.44)

Example 2 (2024-08-19):
- History starts at 68.90 and ends at 72.52 (last 18 days)
- This history shows an upward trend from 68.86 to 72.52
- Model forecasts are again generally higher than true outcomes
- Day 1: model 73.34 vs true 73.14 (+0.20)
- Day 5: model 72.72 vs true 70.49 (+2.23)
- Day 10: model 74.55 vs true 70.43 (+4.12)

Example 3 (2025-03-27):
- Very similar to Example 1, just 1 day earlier

- Model forecasts remain consistently above true outcomes
- First day shows a small overestimation of +0.12
- By day 5, the difference has grown to +2.29
